newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Businessman John Elliott and President of Australian Football League team Carlton, has expressed concern over the media's coverage of racial vilification in the code. Carlton does not wish the media to go overboard on the matter, but the issue looks likey to continue with another hearing this week for alleged vilification. Page 25.

Australian triathletes have dominated the second round of the triathlon World Cup held in Auckland yesterday by winning both the men's and women's divisions. Miles Stewart defeated first round winner Chris McCormack and Melbourne's Emma Carney won the women's division, with Australian women achieving the top three places. Page 27.

South Melbourne have defeated the Melbourne Knights 4-1 in the first round of the elimination final of the National Soccer League. Souths won unexpectedly on the Knights home ground, with the return match next week. Page 29.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Two matches remain in round nine of the Super League competition. Brisbane play Canterbury and Canberra face the Perth Reds to complete the round tonight, with Brisbane looking to get back up from their first loss of the season last weekend. Page 27.

The Sydney Kings basketball team have now lost all but one of their four games after losing to Townsville 91-97 on the weekend. Kings coach Alan Black believes the team must "get their act together now", or face missing the play-offs at the end of the seson. Page 29.

Marconi has defeated Adelaide City in the first round of the National Soccer League's elimination semi-final. Adelaide will face a tough job of overcoming the three-goal advantage in next week's return match. Page 30.
THE AGE

The Melbourne Tigers basketball team have called the national body's decision to rule Mark Bradtke ineligible to play on the weekend as "bureaucratic nonsense". Basketball Australia claim Bradtke had not received the appropriate clearance after a season playing in America. Page Sport2.

Hawthorn may request the Australian Football League to investigate the cause of an eye injury to Brendan Krummel after the player suffered internal bleeding to the eye. Shortly after the incident that caused the injury, Sydney Swans opponent Jason Mooney was charged with head-butting. Page Sport2.

Australian Football League team newcomers Port Adelaide is in the top eight after an impressive performance in defeating Brisbane by two points. Port was tipped to finish last in their debut year, but are surprising many with a strong early performance. age Sport5.
THE HERALD SUN

Ford driver Glenn Seton is leading the Australian Touring Car Championship after winning three races at yesterday's round at Sandown. Russell Ingall won the first two rounds of the championship, but is now runner-up to Seton. Page 92.

Geelong's Australian Football League win over Carlton yesterday has been soured with news that star ruckman John Barnes will miss eight weeks with a broken arm. Geelong defeated Carlton for the first time at Carlton's home ground since 1984. Page 96.

Despite the absence of leading player Mark Bradtke, the Melbourne Tigers basketball side defeated the Melbourne Magic 97-96 in overtime. Bradtke's absence was used as a motivation to the team, who came from behind to win. Page 86.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

After leading the Country rugby league representative side to a win on Friday, coach Tom Raudonikis spurred his club Western Suburbs to an unlikely win over Australian Rugby League leaders Manly. Wests won 19-16 in a momentous win at Campbelltown Sports Gound. Page 35.

Super League newcomers the Adelaide Rams continued their run of upset wins with a defeat of highly-rated Penrith yesterday. Adelaide came from 14-2 behind to defeat Penrith 22-16, as four injuries to senior Penrith players helped their cause. Page 33.

The Australian Jockey Club Principal Club will undergo a name change this week to avoid confusion with the Australian Jockey Club. The new body is likely to be called the NSW Thoroughbred Racing Council.
